fields.label: Apportionment method
fields.value: New York State uses a single receipts factor (100% sales factor) to apportion business income and capital. The business apportionment factor fraction consists of New York State receipts, net income, and net gains divided by everywhere receipts, net income, and net gains.
fields.source_citation: 2025 Form CT-3-I, Instructions for Form CT-3
fields.quote: If you fail to properly complete Part 6 , we may impose a 100% business apportionment factor.

fields.label: Sales sourcing (services and intangibles)
fields.value: New York requires market-based sourcing for receipts from services and intangibles. Services are sourced starting with where the benefit is received, while receipts from intangibles and digital products are sourced based on where the property is used or the customer's primary use location.
fields.quote: Receipts from sale of, license to use, or granting of remote access to digital products Line 7 For Article 9-A apportionment purposes, the term digital product generally means any property or service, or combination thereof, of whatever nature delivered to the purchaser through the use of wire, cable, fiber-optic, laser, microwave, radio wave, satellite or similar successor media, or any combination of these.

fields.label: Special industry rules
fields.value: Special rules apply to railroad, trucking, and omnibus businesses (revenue miles), vessels (working days), aviation, pipeline gas transmission, financial transactions and broker-dealers, and publishing and broadcasting. Qualified financial instruments can also elect an 8% fixed percentage method.

fields.label: Forms
fields.value: Corporate apportionment is computed on Form CT-3, Part 6 for separate C corporations, Form CT-3-A, Part 6 for combined groups, and Form CT-3-S, Part 3 for S corporations. Metropolitan Transportation Business Tax surcharge filers use Form CT-3-M, Part 6.
fields.source_citation: 2025 Form CT-3-I, Instructions for Form CT-3
fields.quote: If you have no receipts required to be included in the denominator of the apportionment factor, you must mark the box at the beginning of Form CT-3, Part 6 , Calculation of business apportionment factor .

fields.label: Sales/use tax: economic nexus
fields.value: An out-of-state seller must register as a sales tax vendor if cumulative gross receipts from sales of tangible personal property delivered into New York State exceed $500,000 and the business conducts more than 100 sales of tangible personal property delivered into the state. This threshold is evaluated over the immediately preceding four sales tax quarters.
fields.source_citation: Registration requirement for businesses with no physical presence in New York State
fields.quote: Information How does a business determine if it meets the registration requirements? To determine if you are required to register, see if you had more than $500,000 in sales of tangible personal property delivered in the state and conducted more than 100 sales of tangible personal property delivered in the state in the immediately preceding four sales tax quarters.

fields.label: P.L. 86-272
fields.value: A foreign corporation is exempt from Article 9-A franchise tax if its activities are limited to the solicitation of orders for sales of tangible personal property filled from outside New York, and it is not required to file Form CT-3 if it exceeds the economic nexus threshold solely through protected activities. However, interactive online activities with New York customers beyond solicitation forfeit P.L. 86-272 protection.
fields.source_citation: Tax tips for avoiding common filing errors for general business corporations
fields.quote: Tips for foreign corporations and corporate partners Public Law (PL) 86-272 foreign corporations are exempt from the corporate franchise tax Foreign corporations that are not part of a combined group that are disclaiming tax liability in NYS based on PL 86-272 are not required to file Form CT-3 or pay tax on any base under the corporate franchise tax, including the fixed dollar minimum tax or file any other form.

fields.value: Personal income tax rate schedules were revised for middle-class rate reductions effective January 1, 2026, under Chapter 59 of the Laws of 2025. The supplemental wage withholding rate is 11.70%.

fields.label: Corporate income/franchise tax
fields.value: General business corporations pay 6.50% on business income, or 7.25% if the income base exceeds $5,000,000 (0.00% for qualified manufacturers and 4.875% for QETCs), alongside a 0.1875% capital base tax. A receipts-based fixed dollar minimum tax ranges from $25 to $200,000.

fields.label: Sales and use tax
fields.value: The state sales and use tax rate is 4.00%, with local jurisdictions adding local sales and use taxes. An additional 0.375% applies within the Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District.
fields.quote: JURISDICTION/RATE LOOKUP BY ADDRESS Sales tax rates The combined sales and use tax rate equals the state rate (currently 4%) plus any local tax rate imposed by a city, county, or school district.

fields.label: Individual due date and extension
fields.value: Individual returns for calendar-year filers are due on or before April 15. Taxpayers can receive an automatic six-month extension to October 15 by filing Form IT-370 with full payment of estimated tax on or before the due date.
fields.quote: If you are required to file Form Y-203 , Yonkers Nonresident Earnings Tax Return , we will automatically extend the time to file when you file Form IT-370.

fields.label: Pass-through entity tax (PTET)
fields.value: Available as an annual election made online between January 1 and March 15 (next business day if March 15 is a weekend or legal holiday). Eligible: partnerships and New York S corporations; not sole proprietorships, trusts, non-profit corporations or other corporations. The election is irrevocable after the due date and may be revoked until the due date of the first estimated payment.
fields.source_citation: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance, Pass-through entity tax (PTET)

fields.label: Withholding and estimated payments
fields.value: Partnerships and NY S corporations must make quarterly estimated payments for nonresidents on Forms IT-2658 and CT-2658, due April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15, unless the partner's estimated tax is $300 or less or an exemption is filed. Electing PTET entities pay quarterly installments on March 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15 totaling the lesser of 90% of the current year PTET or 100% of the prior year PTET.
fields.source_citation: Instructions for Form CT-2658, Report of Estimated Tax for Corporate Partners Tax Year 2026
fields.quote: Estimated tax payments are not required for any partner whose New York State estimated tax required to be paid for the tax year by the partnership is $300 or less.

fields.label: Key forms
fields.value: Primary individual forms include Form IT-201 and Form IT-203. Corporate returns use Form CT-3, Form CT-3-A, or Form CT-3-S, while partnerships file Form IT-204 and Form IT-204-LL.
fields.source_citation: Frequently asked questions about the pass-through entity tax (PTET)
fields.quote: The nonresident partners must file individual New York State personal income tax returns (Form IT-203, Nonresident and Part-Year Resident Income Tax Return ) to claim the PTET credit.
